page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Running head at the top, left of centre, with the page number at the top right. Section heading "SECT. IIII." centred in the middle of the page. Signature "P 4" at the foot left, below the last line. No margin notes.

main_text.p: Quisquis ergo vendicat sibi jus dispen-sandi in Juramento, assumit sibi potestatem divinam, erigendo sibi tribunal in foro interno, & exercendo dominium in hominum conscientias. Et est ipsa dispensatio invalida, & de jure nulla: sicut sententia prolata a Judice in loro [?] non suo, quia prolata est a non Judice, est ad omnem juris effectum invalida.
main_text.head: SECT. IIII.
main_text.p: Torquent hic se mirum in modum Dispensationum Patroni, ut primi argumenti (quod sibimet unum objicere solent) vim declinare videantur. Sudant nimirum hoc saxum versando, (tuendam enim sibi vident utcunque Papæ hac ex parte authoritatem, ne culinæ suæ male sit) nec tamen proficiunt hilum: dum quo se solide tueantur non habent, nec inter ipsos adhuc unquam convenire potuit, quo jure Papa hanc sibi arroget dispensandi potestatem. Quod vel unum malæ defensionis conscientiam arguit. Quemadmodum enim in bello suscipiendo, sic & in exercenda potestate, causa quæ parum constanter assignatur, facile præsumitur esse parum justa.

page.notes: The word "objicere" is struck through by a stroke in the print. "loro" in the sentence "in loro non suo" is doubtful; it may be a printing error for "loco" or similar, and is marked [?]. The page's first line is a continuation from the previous page. The last line "justa." sits beside the signature "P 4". The "s" long s is rendered as plain s throughout.
